params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

params.name: email
params.description: Filter by one or more email addresses.

params.name: id
params.description: Filter by one or more user IDs.

params.name: include
params.description: Additional information to include for each user.

items.docs: Returns a list of users within the enterprise account. Results can be filtered by user IDs or email addresses, and can include collaboration details.

params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

items.docs: Deletes one or more users from the enterprise account by their user IDs. This permanently removes the users and their data.

info.name: Airtable Remove a User from Enterprise

params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user to remove.

items.docs: Removes a user from the enterprise account. Optionally, a replacement user can be specified to take over shared resources. The response includes details about affected shared and unshared resources.

params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

items.docs: Claims one or more users into the enterprise account, setting their management status to either managed or unmanaged.

params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

items.docs: Updates the managed or unmanaged status for one or more users in the enterprise account.

info.name: Airtable Grant Admin Access to Users

params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

items.docs: Grants enterprise admin access to one or more users, allowing them to manage the enterprise account through the Admin panel and API.

info.name: Airtable Revoke Admin Access from Users

params.name: enterpriseAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier of the enterprise account (starts with 'ent').

items.docs: Revokes enterprise admin access from one or more users. The users retain their regular enterprise membership but lose admin privileges.

params.name: filter
params.description: SCIM filter expression (e.g., userName eq "user@example.com"). Supports eq operator on userName.

params.name: startIndex
params.description: The 1-based index of the first result to return.

params.name: count
params.description: The maximum number of results to return per page.

items.docs: Returns a paginated list of SCIM user resources. Supports filtering by user attributes and pagination using startIndex and count parameters per the SCIM 2.0 specification.
Provisions a new user in Airtable through the SCIM protocol. The user will be added to the enterprise account. SSO must be configured as Airtable does not allow setting passwords through SCIM.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the SCIM user resource.

items.docs: Retrieves a single SCIM user resource by its unique identifier. Returns the complete user profile including name, email, and active status.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the SCIM user resource.

items.docs: Replaces a SCIM user resource entirely. All attributes are overwritten with the values in the request body. This is a full replacement, not a partial update.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the SCIM user resource.

items.docs: Partially updates a SCIM user resource using SCIM PATCH operations. Supports add, replace, and remove operations on user attributes. Commonly used to activate or deactivate users.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the SCIM user resource.

items.docs: Permanently deletes a SCIM user resource from the enterprise account. The user will lose access to all Airtable resources associated with the enterprise.
